title: Brown-Butter Chocolate Chip Cookies
description: Crisp edges, chewy middles, deep toffee flavor from browned butter.

tools.name: Light-colored saucepan
tools.notes: A pale interior helps you see the butter browning.

ingredients.name: semisweet chocolate chips or chopped chocolate

steps.heading: Brown the butter
steps.body: Melt {ingredient:butter} in the {tool:saucepan} over medium heat. Once foamy, swirl until the milk solids turn deep amber and smell nutty, 5–7 minutes. Pour into the {tool:bowl-large} — scrape the brown bits in too.

notes.body: Browned butter goes from amber to burnt in seconds. Pull it off the heat the moment it smells like toffee.
The amber color is Maillard browning of the milk solids. That's the flavor you're paying for.

steps.heading: Cool the butter
steps.body: Let the butter cool until just warm to the touch — it should still be liquid but not hot.

notes.body: Hot butter scrambles the eggs and melts the sugar into a glassy puddle. Patience here pays off.

steps.heading: Sugars and eggs
steps.body: To the cooled {ingredient:butter}, whisk in {ingredient:brown-sugar} and {ingredient:white-sugar} until glossy. Whisk in {ingredient:eggs} one at a time, then {ingredient:vanilla}. Keep whisking for 30 seconds — the batter should ribbon off the whisk.

notes.body: Whisking aerates the eggs and dissolves the sugar, giving the cookies a crackled, glossy top.

steps.heading: Combine and fold in chips
steps.body: Switch to the {tool:spatula}. Add the dry mix and fold until just barely streaky. Add {ingredient:chips} and fold to distribute.

notes.body: Stop folding before the flour fully disappears — you'll finish mixing on the next pass with the chips.

steps.heading: Chill
steps.body: Cover the dough and refrigerate. This is not optional.

notes.body: Up to 48 hours in the fridge gives an even deeper toffee flavor.
Chilling lets the flour hydrate evenly and keeps the cookies from spreading into thin discs.

steps.heading: Preheat and scoop
steps.body: Preheat the oven to 375°F / 190°C. Line a {tool:sheet} with {tool:parchment}. Use the {tool:scoop} to portion balls of dough, leaving 2 inches between.

steps.heading: Bake
steps.body: Bake until the edges are set and golden but the centers still look underdone, 10–12 minutes. Sprinkle with {ingredient:flake-salt} the moment they come out.

notes.body: Pull them a touch early — they finish setting on the hot pan.
Bang the pan on the counter twice as soon as they come out for that bakery-style ripple.
